setup: Set the pins at your chosen squat depth
Get under the bar in a full squat
Bar on your upper back, feet set
execution: Drive up from a dead stop
Push your back into the bar
Stand up fully, then lower to the pins
Let the bar settle before the next rep
faults: Don't bounce the bar off the pins
Don't let your hips shoot up first
Don't lose your brace at the bottom

notes: Work inside a power rack. The pins or safety straps hold the bar at the bottom, so you can set it down there if a rep fails.
Check both pins are at the same hole and fully locked before loading the bar.
Getting into position under a bar at the bottom of a squat is awkward; practise with an empty bar first.
Starting from a dead stop is harder than a normal squat, so use less weight than your usual squat. Logged as total bar weight.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Box squat
regressions.reason: A box gives a set depth with less awkward setup.

regressions.name: Paused back squat
regressions.reason: A pause at the bottom without the dead-stop start.

progressions.name: Lower pin height
progressions.reason: A deeper start makes the drive harder. Record pin height as a modifier.

substitutions.name: Paused back squat
substitutions.reason: Same goal of strength out of the bottom with no rebound.

substitutions.name: Back squat
substitutions.reason: The full lift; loads aren't comparable.

substitutions.name: Smith machine squat
substitutions.reason: Squat with built-in catches; can also be started from the stops.

substitutions.name: Front squat
substitutions.reason: More upright squat with the bar in front.
